Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and the few numbers we need to size Dedicated / Private options vs Hosted. I put a short sizing sheet attached (20260528-sizing_qs.xlsx) — if you can fill the highlighted cells that will speed things up.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary constraint: data residency & PII (customer names/transactions) — you indicated corp policy prefers VPC-only or Private on-prem for now.
- Secondary: desire for predictable latency (p95 < 300ms for short prompts) and cost visibility.
- Workload: mix of short transactional prompts + occasional long-context retrieval.

Quick asks to validate the sizing sheet (we only need the bold items to start):
- Typical TPS (queries/sec) and peak TPS during bursts (examples from last week are fine).
- Typical token mix: % under 256 tokens, % 256–1024, % >1024 and an estimated avg tokens per request.
- Concurrency target (how many simultaneous UI users/requests you need served at p95).
- Model family & size you expect to run (open-13B, 34B, etc.) — if unsure, tell us the use-case and we can recommend.

Notes on options (very short):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, good for lower security needs.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (predictable throughput + isolation) — good middle ground, supports stricter controls and SLA.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for customers who must control network + keys; higher operational lift but best for strict compliance.

Next steps:
1) If you can return the sizing sheet, I’ll loop in Aditya (infra) and Lauren (solutions) to propose concrete GPU SKUs and preliminary cost.
2) If preferred, we can schedule a 30-min sizing session — propose Tue or Wed next week.

Thanks — I’ll hold off on pricing until we have the token/TPS numbers.

Best,

Kimberly —

Thanks for the notes and the sheet. Filling it out now and attaching a short sample of last week's traffic (traffic_sample.csv) so you have real numbers to look at. Quick answers inline below: 

- TPS: steady-state ~12 TPS, peak bursts up to ~120 TPS (10–15 minute bursts).
- Token mix (approx): 70% <256 tokens, 25% 256–1024 tokens, 5% >1024 tokens. Avg tokens per request ~340.
- Concurrency: we typically expect to support ~25 concurrent interactive users at peak; backend async jobs add another ~20 concurrent requests during retrieval-heavy windows.
- Models: evaluating two families — an open 13B (for lower-latency UI) and a 33B variant for higher quality batch reranks. If Dedicated is the route, we prefer GPU-level isolation (not multi-tenant hosted).
- Compliance: SOC2 in scope; ideally VPC with customer-managed keys.

We lean toward Dedicated or Private depending on cost and operational effort. If you can send SKU guidance (rough count of GPUs / instance types) and a ballpark monthly cost range, that will help our procurement team.

Kim / Lauren —

Thanks for the forward and the traffic sample. Based on the profile (avg ~340 tokens, steady 12 TPS, 120 TPS bursts, ~45 concurrent peak) and model candidates (13B interactive + 33B batch), here are concise recommendations for Dedicated pathing and a fallback note for Private: 

1) Quick sizing guidance (Dedicated SKU options):
- Primary interactive (13B): 1 H100-80GB (or 2x A100-80GB in split-shard config) can handle ~80–100 short-request TPS with batching and prefix caching. For the burst profile up to 120 TPS we recommend starting with 2x H100-80GB in a small reserved pool (gives headroom for concurrent 25 interactive users + small batch jobs).
- Secondary batch/33B rerank: a single A100-80GB node can be used for scheduled reranks; if you need concurrent real-time 33B, consider 2x A100-80GB or a mixed pool with one H100 for heavy-quality paths.

2) Concurrency & batching notes:
- Target concurrency per shard: plan for 8–12 concurrent streams on H100 for 13B interactive with dynamic batching. That maps to the above 2x H100 recommendation to hit 120 TPS burst with p95 latency targets.
- Batch size tuning: use adaptive batching (target batch 4–8) for short prompts; larger batches for long-context reranks.

3) Token mix & cache recommendations:
- With 70% short prompts, enable prefix/KV caching aggressively — this reduces effective compute for repeat prefixes and improves token throughput.
- Quantization: FP16 or AMP kicks in on H100; evaluate FP16 first, int8 if memory-bound and accuracy acceptable.

4) Cost ballpark (monthly, very rough):
- Dedicated pool (2x H100 reserved, moderate utilization): order-of-magnitude $40k–$65k/month (includes reserved GPU, network, reserved capacity premium).
- Adding A100 node for batch rerank: additional $8k–$18k/month depending on commit. (These are placeholders — we can get exact pricing once we pick commit term and region.)

5) Private / VPC considerations:
- If procurement requires customer-managed keys and on-prem VPC-only, expect additional setup time (2–6 weeks) and O&M overhead; costs will be higher due to infra and support. Still doable — we should prepare a Private scoping doc if they push in that direction.

6) Deliverable: I attached a 1–2 page PDF with the SKU rationale and a couple of diagrams (dedicated_sku_recs.pdf). If this looks reasonable, Kimberly, I suggest we:
- Send the PDF to Finodev procurement along with an invite for a 30-min sizing Q&A (I can join)
- Optionally provide a short trial: 1-week dedicated pool pilot with capped commit to validate real throughput.

If you want, I can also run a quick perf sim against the traffic_sample.csv to produce a predicted p95 latency table for both 13B and 33B — that will make the procurement ask easier.

Aditya
